question: Which disease is transmitted to humans by a flavivirus that can cause inflammation in the brain?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Japanese Encephalitis__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Japanese encephalitis virus causes a brain infection.
 
• Although most illnesses cause little to no symptoms, brain inflammation does occur on occasion. 
 
• Symptoms in these cases can include headache, vomiting, fever, confusion, and seizures. This happens 5 to 15 days after infection.
 
• It is a virus from the** flavivirus **family.
 
• **Flavivirus**
 
 
• Flavivirus, renamed Orthoflavivirus in 2023, is a genus of **positive-strand RNA viruses** in the family Flaviviridae. The genus includes the West Nile virus, dengue virus, tick-borne encephalitis virus, yellow fever virus, Zika virus, and several other viruses which may cause encephalitis, as well as insect-specific flaviviruses (ISFs) such as cell fusing agent virus (CFAV), Palm Creek virus (PCV), and Parramatta River virus (PaRV).
 
 
 
• Japanese encephalitis is the most common form of encephalitis in Southeast Asia.
 
• In the past, outbreaks have occurred in China, Korea, Japan, Taiwan, and Thailand, but the disease has been mostly contained by vaccination. Epidemics also occur on occasion in Vietnam, Cambodia, Myanmar, India, Nepal, and Malaysia.
 
• JEV is primarily transmitted by mosquitos, especially those of the **Culex genus**. As spread through a vector(*Culex *mosquito), it is also called a vector-borne disease. 
 
• Blood or cerebrospinal fluid examination is used to make a diagnosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Anthrax**

 
 
• Anthrax causes a fatal blood disease known as sorter's disease.
 
• It is a rare infectious disease caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis.
 
• It occurs naturally around the world in wild and domestic hoofed animals, especially cattle, sheep, goats, camels, and antelopes.
 
• It can also occur in humans when they are exposed to the bacterium, usually through handling animals or animals' hides.
 
• There are 3 forms of anthrax infection: cutaneous (skin), inhalation (lungs), and gastrointestinal (stomach and intestine).
 
 
 
• Leptospirosis ​
 
 
• Leptospirosis is caused by bacteria.
 
• It is a zoonotic disease and affects both animals and humans.
 
• It is transmitted by the urine and feces of animals.
 
• The urine-borne disease of rats is Leptospirosis.
 
• It causes fever, chill, vomiting, and diarrhea.
 
• It is treated by taking antibiotics and drinking a lot of water.
